groups.intro:
Whether and how the state credentials this profession — the regulatory model,
credential type, issuing authority, entry requirements (education, exams, age,
character), fees, renewal, continuing education, and reciprocity.

fields.meaning: Whether the state requires a credential to practice this profession.

example.quote: A person may not practice medicine, podiatry, or osteopathy in the state unless the person is licensed under this chapter

fields.meaning: Free-text name of the board/agency that issues the credential (the structured form is `regulatory_authority`).

example.quote: the governor shall appoint a board of medical examiners, to be known as the State Medical Board

fields.meaning: Structured decomposition of the issuing authority — name, type (standalone board / shared board / division / department / joint), and any umbrella agency it sits within. Populated alongside the legacy free-text issuing_authority for back-compat.
Canonical name of the immediate authority (e.g., 'State Board of Podiatry').

example.quote: the governor shall appoint a board of medical examiners, to be known as the State Medical Board

fields.meaning: Structural classification of the immediate authority.

example.quote: the governor shall appoint a board of medical examiners, to be known as the State Medical Board, consisting of five physicians licensed in the state

fields.meaning: Higher-level agency that contains the immediate authority, if any. Example: 'Division of Occupations and Professions, Department of Commerce'. Null for standalone boards that don't sit inside a larger department.

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Minimum age (years) to hold the credential, if the statute sets one.

example.quote: Is at least twenty-one (21) years of age

fields.meaning: Whether the statute conditions licensure on good moral character / fitness.

example.quote: if the commission finds that the applicant is of good moral character and has been duly certified by the board, the commission shall issue to such applicant a license

fields.meaning: Education entry requirement — degree, level, accreditation, and any tiers.

example.value: Certificate of graduation from a legally chartered medical school accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association
example.quote: submit a certificate of graduation from a legally chartered medical school accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Assoc

example.value: Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association
example.quote: accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association

fields.meaning: The comparable education FLOOR as a normalized rung. Populate whenever licensure is gated on a degree; null only if the statute is silent on education.

example.quote: submit a certificate of graduation from a legally chartered medical school accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Assoc

fields.meaning: How the statute decides a school counts. national_accreditor=a named national program accreditor (ACOE/CODA/ACEND/LCME/CPME). regional_accreditor='regionally accredited college or university'. board_approved='approved by the board' (discretionary state gate). unspecified=says 'accredited' with no basis named, or silent.

example.quote: accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association

fields.meaning: True if the statute pegs the education requirement to a NATIONAL CREDENTIAL (e.g. 'registered by CDR', 'passed the NBEO') rather than (or in addition to) a stated degree — such a state inherits whatever that national body currently requires.

example.quote: submit a certificate of graduation from a legally chartered medical school accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Assoc

fields.meaning: Per-tier floors when the statute sets different education levels for different license classes, or phases the floor in by date. Omit/null when there is a single floor. `degree_level` still records the overall floor across all tiers.
Which class/date this floor applies to — e.g. 'licensed dietitian', 'certified nutritionist', 'applicants on or after 2024-01-01'.

Normalized education floor, low -> high. Resolved to the rung even when
the statute uses verbiage ('six college years' -> doctorate, 'or equivalent
degree' -> the named level). Professional/clinical doctorates (OD, DDS, MD,
DPM) are `doctorate`.
ISO date when this floor takes effect, for date-phased tiers (e.g. '2024-01-01'). Null otherwise.
Supervised practice / residency / apprenticeship required after the degree.

example.quote: submit a certificate from a recognized hospital or hospitals certifying that the applicant has satisfactorily performed the duties of resident physician or intern for a period of

fields.meaning: ALWAYS populate (required_by_statute / embedded_in_credential / none) unless the governing statute is absent from the corpus. Disambiguates a blank `required`: 'none' (truly no requirement) vs 'embedded_in_credential' (the accredited degree the statute points to carries the supervised hours).

example.quote: submit a certificate from a recognized hospital or hospitals certifying that the applicant has satisfactorily performed the duties of resident physician or intern for a period of

fields.meaning: e.g. '24 months', '1 year', '2,000 hours' (free text — units vary)

example.value: one year (pre-1995 graduates) or two years (post-1995 graduates); three years for foreign medical graduates
example.quote: one year if the applicant graduated from medical school before January 1, 1995 ... two years if the applicant graduated from medical school on or after January 1, 1995

fields.meaning: e.g. 'podiatric residency', 'accounting work experience', 'AXP'

example.quote: satisfactorily performed the duties of resident physician or intern

fields.meaning: Examinations required for the credential (one entry per exam).

example.value: Board sets subjects; examination may be waived for licensure by credentials under AS 08.64.250

fields.meaning: Where the exam is administered / who owns it — e.g. 'NBPME (national)', 'state board (in-state)', 'NCLEX-RN (national)'. Use the statute's language; null if the source doesn't say.
Max attempts allowed before re-qualification. Null if not specified.
How the credential is renewed — interval and any conditions.
Most states are 1 or 2

example.quote: Licenses shall be renewed biennially on the dates set by the department with the approval of the respective board.

fields.meaning: License renewal fee in US dollars (integer). Many statutes leave the amount to the board's discretion — leave null in that case.

example.quote: For licenses that expire on or after January 1, 2024, the biennial renewal fee shall be one thousand one hundred fifty-one dollars ($1,151).

fields.meaning: Continuing-education requirement to keep the credential active.

example.quote: the board shall promote a high degree of competence in the practice of medicine, osteopathy, and podiatry by requiring every licensee of medicine, osteopathy, and podiatry in the state to fulfill cont

the board shall not renew, reinstate, or reactivate a license of a physician unless the physician presents evidence that the physician has completed thirty CME credit hours within the compliance perio
Before a license may be renewed, the licensee shall submit evidence to the board or its designee that continuing education requirements prescribed by regulations adopted by the board have been met.

fields.meaning: Specific topical CE requirements, e.g. ['1.5 hrs opioid', 'ethics']

value: pain management and opioid use and addiction (not less than two hours in the two years preceding renewal)
example.quote: Continuing education requirements must include not less than two hours of education in pain management and opioid use and addiction in the two years preceding an application for renewal of a license

fields.meaning: Whether/how the state recognizes out-of-state credentials (endorsement/reciprocity).

example.quote: The board may waive the examination requirement and license by credentials if the physician, osteopath, or podiatry applicant meets the requirements of AS 08.64.200, 08.64.205, or 08.64.209, submits p

fields.meaning: Free-form summary

example.value: Applicant must meet education and training requirements, submit proof of continued competence, pay required fee, and hold an active license from another U.S. state/territory or Canadian province/territory, or have passed an examination specified by the board.
example.quote: The board may waive the examination requirement and license by credentials if the physician, osteopath, or podiatry applicant meets the requirements of AS 08.64.200, 08.64.205, or 08.64.209, submits p

fields.meaning: Profession-specific advisory body sitting alongside the main licensing board, when one exists. Populated for states that delegate licensure to a generic board and add a specialty advisory committee.
True if a profession-specific advisory body exists alongside the main licensing board. False if the licensing board itself is profession-specific (no separate advisory body needed).

example.quote: the governor shall appoint a board of medical examiners, to be known as the State Medical Board, consisting of five physicians licensed in the state

fields.meaning: Name of the advisory board, e.g. 'Podiatry Advisory Committee'.

example.quote: prior to exercising its power and authority to issue, revoke, or reinstate licenses, or to promulgate rules and regulations, the Medical Licensure Commission shall receive and consider but not be boun

fields.meaning: Authority the advisory board has, in the statute's own words — e.g. 'advisory only', 'rulemaking subject to board approval', 'disciplinary recommendations'. Free text from the statute.

example.value: advisory only — the Medical Licensure Commission shall receive and consider but not be bound by the recommendation of the State Board of Medical Examiners
example.quote: the Medical Licensure Commission shall receive and consider but not be bound by the recommendation of the State Board of Medical Examiners

fields.meaning: Name of a national CERTIFICATION the state recognizes or requires, e.g. 'American Board of Podiatric Surgery (ABPS)' or 'National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (NBPME)'. The certifying body, NOT the association. Null if the statute doesn't reference one.

example.value: National Board of Examiners for Osteopathic Physicians and Surgeons; National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners; American Board of Medical Specialties (for foreign medical graduates)
example.quote: be certified to practice by the National Board of Examiners for Osteopathic Physicians and Surgeons or by the National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners

fields.meaning: Professional ASSOCIATION the state references (e.g. for accreditation or CE provider approval) — 'American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA)', 'American Dental Association (ADA)'. Distinct from the certifying body. Null if not referenced.

example.value: Association of American Medical Colleges; American Medical Association; American Osteopathic Association; Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education
example.quote: accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association

fields.meaning: Which UORF model the state applies to this profession (license / mandatory_cert / registration / etc).

example.quote: A person may not practice medicine, podiatry, or osteopathy in the state unless the person is licensed under this chapter

fields.meaning: What SHAPE of credential does the state issue, independent of whether holding it is mandatory? license / certification / registration / exemption / none. Pairs with is_mandatory to decompose the legacy regulatory_model rung.

example.quote: the board or its executive secretary shall grant a license to the applicant to practice medicine in the state

fields.meaning: Is the credential MANDATORY to practice (or claim the title) in this state? True if practicing without it is prohibited; False if optional (e.g., voluntary certification that only protects the title for those who hold it).

example.quote: A person may not practice medicine, podiatry, or osteopathy in the state unless the person is licensed under this chapter

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict use of the profession's title to licensees? True if unlicensed people may NOT call themselves the protected title (e.g. 'podiatrist', 'CPA').

example.quote: to use or publicly display a title in connection with a person's name including "doctor of medicine," "physician," "M.D.," or "doctor of osteopathic medicine" or "D.O." or a specialist designation inc

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict practice of the profession's scope to licensees? True if performing the scope without a license is prohibited (independent of title use).

example.quote: A person may not practice medicine, podiatry, or osteopathy in the state unless the person is licensed under this chapter

fields.meaning: Grounds on which the board may discipline a licensee. Typical statutes list 5-15.
snake_case key, e.g. 'fraud_in_obtaining_license'
One-line plain-English description

example.value: Secured a license through deceit, fraud, or intentional misrepresentation

fields.meaning: Non-credential regulatory mechanisms (bonding, insurance, establishment regulation) imposed by the state. Obama 2015 framework typology. Independent of credential_type.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to post a bond (funds against which consumer claims can be made)? Independent of whether a credential is also required.

example.quote: The board is authorized to promulgate regulations requiring physicians to obtain professional malpractice liability insurance or a suitable bond or other indemnity against liability for professional m

fields.meaning: Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to carry insurance (e.g., professional liability, surety insurance)?

example.quote: It is unprofessional conduct for a physician and surgeon to fail to provide adequate security by liability insurance, or by participation in an interindemnity trust, for claims by patients arising out

fields.meaning: Does the statute regulate the ESTABLISHMENT / FIRM (e.g., facility license, mandatory inspection of premises) as a route to consumer protection, independent of any practitioner credential?

example.quote: no physician and surgeon shall perform procedures in an outpatient setting using anesthesia, except local anesthesia or peripheral nerve blocks ... unless the setting is specified in Section 1248.1.

fields.meaning: Statutory citations supporting the licensure fields above.

groups.intro:
What the practice act lets (or reserves to) this profession — the defined scope,
authorized methods, drug authority, and any title/scope protection. Skeleton only —
profession-specific scope richness lives in the discovered block.

fields.meaning: Verbatim statutory definition; quote field repeats the value text.

example.value: for a fee, donation or other consideration, to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other mental or physical condition; or to attempt to perform or represent that a person is authorized to perform any of the acts set out in this subparagraph
example.quote: for a fee, donation or other consideration, to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other m

fields.meaning: High-level methods, e.g. ['medical','surgical','mechanical']

example.quote: to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other mental or physical condition

Prescribing via telehealth permitted with conditions.

groups.intro: Fields discovered specifically for this profession (auto-derived from its statutes); they vary profession to profession.

fields.meaning: The distinct license status categories a physician may hold beyond a standard active license, such as inactive, retired, volunteer, temporary, or administrative.

example.quote: A licensee who does not practice in the state may hold an inactive license. A person who practices in the state, however infrequently, shall hold an active license.

fields.meaning: Special additional requirements imposed on graduates of medical schools outside the United States or Canada, such as additional postgraduate training years, ECFMG certification, or separate examination standards.

example.value: Foreign medical graduates (graduates of schools not accredited by AAMC/AMA) must meet requirements of AS 08.64.200(a)(3)-(5) and 08.64.255, complete three years of postgraduate training (or alternative board-approved proof of competency), and pass examinations specified by the board.
example.quote: Applicants who are graduates of medical colleges not accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association shall (1) meet

fields.meaning: The minimum number of years of postgraduate internship or residency training required before a license will be issued to a standard domestic medical school graduate.

example.quote: two years if the applicant graduated from medical school on or after January 1, 1995

fields.meaning: Whether the state requires applicants or licensees to complete specific education in pain management and opioid use and addiction as a condition of licensure or renewal.

example.quote: receive education in pain management and opioid use and addiction, unless the applicant has demonstrated to the satisfaction of the board that the applicant does not currently hold a valid federal Dru

fields.meaning: Statutory limits on the quantity or duration of opioid prescriptions a licensee may issue, including any exceptions for chronic pain, cancer, or palliative care.

example.value: Initial prescription for an opioid may not exceed a seven-day supply for adult outpatients; no opioid prescription may exceed seven days for minors. Exceptions exist for acute medical conditions, chronic pain, cancer pain, palliative care, logistical/travel barriers, or treatment of substance abuse/opioid dependence.
example.quote: A licensee may not issue (1) an initial prescription for an opioid that exceeds a seven-day supply to an adult patient for outpatient use; (2) a prescription for an opioid that exceeds a seven-day sup

fields.meaning: Whether licensees who hold a DEA registration number are required to register with or use the state's prescription drug monitoring program or controlled substance database.

example.quote: require that a licensee who has a federal Drug Enforcement Administration registration number register with the controlled substance prescription database under AS 17.30.200(n)

fields.meaning: Whether physicians providing pain management services must obtain a separate registration or license from the board in addition to their standard medical license.

example.quote: All physicians providing pain management services shall obtain a pain management registration from the board.

fields.meaning: Specific statutory conditions under which a physician may prescribe drugs, including controlled substances, to patients seen only via telehealth rather than in person.

example.value: Board may not impose disciplinary sanctions on a physician for prescribing a non-controlled prescription drug via telehealth if follow-up care is available and records are sent to primary care provider with patient consent. Prescribing controlled substances via telehealth is also permitted if those conditions and opioid limits are met. Prescribing via internet questionnaire or email without a prior physician-patient relationship is prohibited.

example.quote: Physicians who engage in the provision of telehealth medical services to any individual in this state must possess a full and active license to practice medicine or osteopathy issued by the Medical Li

fields.meaning: Whether the state has enacted the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact, enabling eligible physicians to obtain expedited licenses in multiple member states.

example.value: Physician assistants may prescribe drugs (including controlled substances), subject to board regulations on scope of activities and supervising physician responsibilities; prescribing without physical examination is permitted under the same conditions as for physicians.

example.quote: Limit supervision to no more than two (2) graduate registered physicians per supervising physician.
